outcome.answer:
Large language models can improve product recommendations by actively asking for informative preference cues during a conversation and by using those cues to reduce uncertainty in the recommendations [5, 8]. They can also actively gather information by generating or refreshing user context and interaction data from existing histories or catalog data, which is then used to refine recommendations [1, 2, 6, 7, 9, 10].

The closest match for interactive information gathering is conversational recommendation: stage-aware elicitation strategies decide when to ask about attributes versus items [5], and entropy-based interaction generation chooses questions that most reduce uncertainty [8]. Other papers use LLMs more as data or context generators than as question askers, including semantic enrichment of sequences [1], real-time user personas [2], synthetic interactions for sparse or cold-start data [6, 10], live-catalog retrieval refresh [7], and LLM-generated user profiles from histories [9].
